records.title: Pic Shows Three IPS Officers From Same Family? It's a False Claim
records.retrieval_query: Does a photo exist that shows three people identified as Indian Police Service officers together?

passages.P2: # Pic Shows Three IPS Officers From Same Family? It’s a False Claim
passages.P3: ## One of the police officers seen in the viral image, Shrut Kirti Somavanshi, said that the claim is “not true.”
passages.P15: An image showing three officers of the Indian Police Service is doing the rounds with an inspirational message that they belong to the same family.
passages.P16: However, one of the police officers seen in the viral image, Shrut Kirti Somavanshi, told **The Quint** that the claim being made is “not true.”
passages.P18: The photo is being shared with the claim: “Can you imagine Three IPS officers in one family? Yes. Meet this family of two brothers & a sister, all IPS officers. Inspirational! How proud their parents must be (sic).”
passages.P19: The tweet shared by one Nausheen Khan had garnered over 1,000 likes at the time of publishing the story. However, she later issued a clarification.
passages.P20: Several social media users shared the image on Facebook and Twitter with the same claim.
passages.P23: We found several replies on the tweet shared by @DrNausheenKhan with people calling it “fake news”. A user identified the person in extreme left as ‘Shrut Somwanshi’ and said that the other two are his batchmates.
passages.P24: We came across an Instagram post shared by IPS officer Tushar Gupta that carried the same image. The user had tagged the other two people as: Shrut Kirti Somavanshi and Pooja Vashisth.
passages.P25: **The Quint**’s WebQoof team also viewed Tushar Gupta’s Instagram story which showed that Shrut Kirti Somavanshi had called out the viral image saying: “False information, refrain from sharing.”
passages.P26: > Somavanshi told **The Quint** that the claim being made along with the image is not true. “Three of us are batchmates, not siblings,” he added.
passages.P27: We came across a notification published on the website of the Indian Police Service dated 19 December 2018. The notification was regarding the cadre allotments to the candidates allocated to the Indian Police Service on the basis of the results of the Civil Services Examination 2017.
passages.P28: We found the names of the aforementioned IPS officers in the same list, thereby, confirming that they belong to the same batch.
passages.P29: > The list further showed that the home states of the three officers are also different with Tushar belonging to Punjab, Pooja to Haryana and Shrut Kirti to Uttar Pradesh.
passages.P30: Nausheen Khan, who had shared the image with a false claim, later issued a clarification: “Guys, they are not brothers & sisters of the same family as mentioned in the above tweet, however they are Brothers in Uniform, serving one family - the Nation!”
passages.P31:

passages.P32: Evidently, an image of three IPS batch mates is being circulated with a false emotional message that they belong to the same family.

records.title: No, The Three IPS Officers In This Photo Are Not Siblings
records.retrieval_query: Does a photo exist that shows three people identified as Indian Police Service officers together?

passages.P1: # No, The Three IPS Officers In This Photo Are Not Siblings
passages.P2: ## In 2020, BOOM spoke with Shrut Kirti Somavanshi and Tushar Gupta, the IPS officers are seen in the image refuted the viral claim.
passages.P6: An image of three Indian Police Service (IPS) officers photographed together is viral on social media with claims that they are siblings and have cracked the civil service examinations, making their family proud. The Facebook post has been captioned as, “Two brothers and one sister in the same family and IPS. Jai Hind.”
passages.P8: BOOM spoke to Shrut Kirti Somavanshi in September 2020, who is an IPS officer from the Madhya Pradesh Cadre. He rubbished the narrative associated with the viral image and said us that the three of them are neither siblings nor are they related to each other. BOOM ran a reverse image search and found the image was posted on Instagram on August 22, 2020, by Pooja Vashistah, then an IPS probationer of the Haryana cadre. Shrut Kirti Somavanshi and Tushar Gupta were tagged on the image. Tushar Gupta an IPS 2018 batch, from the Punjab cadre, further told us at that time, "the photograph was clicked in an IPS mess after a training session." Gupta also posted the same image on his Instagram profile. BOOM debunked the image first in September, 2020 when it went viral with the same false claims.
